activeCIAtAudit.evidenceBasis: Actual completed logs for both full jobs, not the stale workflow summary.

scope: Source-and-contract audit plus explicitly attached observations; not a completed full-framework conformance or performance run.

statusRules.open: Acceptance remains unproved even if partial APIs or tests exist.
statusRules.in_progress: An identified implementation slice is active; the whole row is not accepted.
statusRules.accepted: Every stated acceptance item has exact-input executed evidence and normal review/CI/main verification; any differences are explicitly accepted.

kindRules.capability: The audited Purity source lacks the stated compositional capability.
kindRules.partial: Some behavior exists; a specific capability or application contract remains open.
kindRules.evidence: Implementation may exist, but the claimed comparison or release behavior lacks sufficient current evidence.

priorityRules.P0: Close current correctness failures or establish comparison integrity before a new competitive claim.
priorityRules.P1: High-impact application capability or evidence needed to choose Purity for demanding reactive work.
priorityRules.P2: Broader composition, developer or release acceptance after the prerequisite slices.

selectionRules: Finish the active implementation PR and main verification first.
Select a gap by application impact and acceptance prerequisites; choose a bounded slice whose own inputs are sufficient, not an entire subsystem rewrite.

Maintain a capability/evidence lane alongside correctness fixes; after the current known correctness fix, complete SV2-001's first paired baseline and the first SV2-015 evidence slice before selecting unrelated cleanup.
Record gap ID, before/after behavior or metric, exact inputs, evidence and remaining acceptance in each substantive PR/monitor update.
Do not convert a merged regression fix or a green Purity-only CI into whole-row acceptance; do not compute a parity percentage.

gates.policy: Retain existing correctness, security, memory and size gates. Any changed standard requires the user's explicit decision.

gaps.title: Frozen comparator and reproducible comparison inputs
gaps.solid: The selected target is rc.18 for core, signals and web, with separately versioned build and router packages.
gaps.purity: Existing benchmark resolves core/signals rc.15, web/compiler/babel-plugin rc.14 and Vite plugin next.50. Its historical results remain valid only for those inputs.
gaps.impact: Without matched versioned inputs, changes cannot establish progress against the agreed Solid v2 target.
acceptance: Resolve and archive exact rc.18 framework/build package versions and integrities in an executable comparison lockfile.
Verify selected client/server export conditions and baseline behavior before collecting results.
Keep old result identities; record changes caused by upgrading the comparator separately from Purity improvements.
gaps.nextSlice: Create an isolated rc.18 comparison fixture using the target metadata; retain the existing benchmark until its adapter and parity checks pass.

evidence.scope: Two fixed rc.18 tarballs and their actual client/engine entries execute four Node observations; the full application/compiler fixture and transitive lockfile remain open.

gaps.title: Reactive correctness, scheduling and effect observations
gaps.solid: Writes normally stage until commit; user effect application is queued and untracked. Effects do not equality-filter a rerun's returned value; a memo can do that.
gaps.purity: State and computed reads update immediately; auto-watch starts eagerly, explicit callbacks skip the first run, and later effects flush in a microtask. The frozen main still samples an explicit source twice during setup; PR #294 addresses that defect.
gaps.impact: Hidden parent subscriptions can lose child callbacks. Intentional same-stack and effect-phase differences affect migrations and DOM-reading effects.
acceptance: Close PR #294 using its exact-head review and original CI gates, then verify main.
Record state/derived/DOM observations after a write, after a microtask and at explicit synchronization points in both implementations.
Exercise diamond dependencies, source-only callback tracking, nested owners, error recovery and disposal; document intentional differences instead of copying API names.
gaps.nextSlice: Finish #294, then retain a small paired contract suite for observable scheduling and ownership behavior.

evidence.scope: Same-stack versus microtask reads, first/followup effect timing, and callback-only dependency isolation at frozen main 58ff714. No DOM phase claim; excludes PR294.

evidence.scope: Both full jobs fail core-all Brotli 40747 > 40704; core-actions 5248 meets its 5248 cap.

gaps.title: Async derivation through the reactive graph
gaps.solid: Async memos accept PromiseLike or AsyncIterable computation results and propagate unresolved reads through downstream derivations.
gaps.purity: compute caches its direct return, including a Promise. resource separately exposes data, loading and error accessors; downstream code handles unresolved values and flags explicitly.
gaps.impact: A fetched value cannot transparently feed an ordinary derived calculation and a pending-aware consumer without application coordination.
acceptance: Use source -> async derivation -> synchronous derivation -> view/effect, with no undefined or Promise delivered as resolved application data.
Supersede A with B and resolve A last; only B may become current.
Define rejection, cancellation, iterator closure and disposal behavior before selecting an API.
gaps.nextSlice: Specify and implement the smallest owned async-derivation contract with deterministic settlement traces.

gaps.title: Client loading, retained content and coordinated reveal
gaps.solid: Loading handles unresolved reads and retains committed content on ordinary refetch; Reveal coordinates boundary slots. isPending describes unrevealed changed state, not every network request.
gaps.purity: Client suspense directly calls view() and does not use its fallback. Resources can already retain prior data during refresh, but applications assemble loading and cross-region consistency themselves.
gaps.impact: A selector and several async panels can expose mismatched versions or lose local state unless the application coordinates them.
acceptance: Initial load shows a fallback; refresh retains a complete prior view and its edited input state.
Two panels settle in reverse order under an explicit reveal policy without mixing subject versions.
Nested rejection, supersession and unmount release owned work; pending feedback has a defined visible contract.
gaps.nextSlice: Build one client async boundary journey after SV2-003; retain explicit limitations for later reveal policies.

gaps.title: Property-granular structured state and keyed adoption
gaps.solid: Stores track property reads through proxies and use draft updates. Derived stores reconcile snapshots by a selected key; ordinary setter replacement is not keyed reconciliation.
gaps.purity: A state is one Object.is-compared value. Nested objects work through replacement or manually composed field signals; there is no public property-granular store/draft/reconciliation facility.
gaps.impact: Nested forms and entity collections require more application state plumbing and can cause broader dependency invalidation.
acceptance: Update one nested property without rerunning unrelated field or row computations.
Add/delete keys and resize/reorder arrays with correct structural subscriptions.
Adopt new server objects with stable IDs while preserving the intended nested identities; enforce public types and disposal behavior.
gaps.nextSlice: Design an optional structured-state entry around a nested form and editable collection, keeping core runtime dependency constraints.

gaps.title: Reactive error fallback and retry/reset boundaries
gaps.solid: Errored replaces a failed reactive/render subtree, supplies reset, and lets fallback failures reach a parent boundary. Event errors are a separate responsibility.
gaps.purity: Owned later watch failures reach onError, recovery work is owned, computeds can recover, and resources expose error/retry. There is no general client fallback/reset subtree boundary; handler throws are logged.
gaps.impact: Applications must compose retry UI, subtree replacement and nested fallback escalation themselves.
acceptance: A rejected derived value selects the nearest error fallback while sibling UI continues.
A changed input or explicit reset restores the subtree and disposes failed/recovery work once.
A throwing fallback reaches a defined outer boundary; event-handler failures are tested separately.
gaps.nextSlice: Extend the existing ownership/error contract to one explicit client fallback/reset journey.

gaps.title: Async transaction visibility and optimistic overlays
gaps.solid: Generator-based actions hold normal writes across transaction-safe yields; optimistic signals/stores expose tentative overlays that settle with the action.
gaps.purity: optimistic already offers apply/rollback, invalidation and settlement callbacks; resource.mutate invalidates an old fetch. batch controls synchronous scheduling, not graph-wide writes across async work.
gaps.impact: Keeping related authoritative values coherent while showing tentative edits is application code.
acceptance: Two authoritative values changed around async work remain a coherent committed view.
An explicit tentative value appears promptly and settles or rolls back exactly once.
Define overlapping operations and disposal without claiming general server-side business conflict resolution.
gaps.nextSlice: Add a controlled two-field mutation journey and document which transaction guarantees Purity will provide.

gaps.title: Current keyed position and editing-state preservation
gaps.solid: Custom-key For supplies item and current-index accessors; positional mode supplies an item accessor and fixed slot index.
gaps.purity: each preserves keyed row identity and updates item accessors, but its renderer receives a creation-time numeric index. Position-keyed reuse is expressible with the index as key. Multi-root native movement was fixed in #291; focus preservation has a documented fallback limit.
gaps.impact: Ordinal labels or position-based callbacks can become stale after a keyed reorder; editing focus needs a platform-specific contract.
acceptance: Prepend, reverse and replace same-ID objects while node references, local input values and current-position actions stay correct.
Cover both native moveBefore and fragment fallback with explicit focus/selection expectations.
Verify reorder does not dispose retained rows and removal/unmount releases owned work once.
gaps.nextSlice: Specify current-position usage and add the focused-editing scenario to existing production fixtures.

gaps.title: Independent SSR boundary progress
gaps.solid: The streaming renderer flushes a shell and emits settled boundary fragments; reveal policy must be selected when checking sibling progress.
gaps.purity: Deferred SSR views are queued and awaited sequentially. An earlier blocked boundary delays starting a later view, while request cancellation, deadlines and backpressure controls already exist.
gaps.impact: A fast summary or sidebar can wait behind unrelated slow work.
acceptance: Keep the first sibling blocked and let a later sibling become usable before releasing it under the natural-progress contract.
Exercise nesting, rejection, deadlines, request abort, slow readers and serialization failure.
Preserve bounded buffering, request-local resource state and existing retention controls.
gaps.nextSlice: Add a blocked-first/fast-second stream trace, then implement independent scheduling without weakening request lifetime guarantees.

gaps.title: Interactivity during streaming and hydration source policies
gaps.solid: Hydration adopts server DOM and serialized state with explicit server/hybrid/client source policies. The selected streaming integration must be exercised for early interactivity.
gaps.purity: DOM adoption and resource priming exist. The supported full-page path hydrates after the stream closes; the starter sends its client module in the suffix after the body. Islands already replay ordinary first activation, with manually supplied entry thunks.
gaps.impact: An early-painted shell may wait for the final slow region before its handlers are available.
acceptance: With one boundary still pending, an already painted shell control and ready region respond correctly.
Preserve node identity, pre-hydration input edits, resource fetch counts, nonce/CSP behavior and mismatch diagnostics.
Exercise conditional/lazy/streamed islands without duplicate imports or wrong view selection; record trusted-activation limits.
gaps.nextSlice: Specify a supported early-hydration protocol and prove one blocked-stream interaction before widening the claim.

gaps.title: Router, server functions and application composition
gaps.solid: Compare the named v2 router, web server-function support and Vite start-mode stack. SolidStart 2.1.0 targets Solid 1 and is excluded from this v2 baseline.
gaps.purity: Route manifests, layouts, loaders, cancellation, native/enhanced forms, server actions and invalidation exist. The mixed-delivery starter deliberately uses document navigation; applications assemble SPA navigation when wanted.
gaps.impact: A team needs a coherent installed application journey, not a list of separate primitives.
acceptance: Run back/forward, stale navigation, route errors/redirects/statuses and header handling in the same installed application.
Verify no-JS POST, enhanced field errors/retry/input retention, write invalidation and server-only stripping.
Choose document or SPA navigation explicitly and pin the v2-compatible ecosystem packages used for comparison.
gaps.nextSlice: Use one realistic installed application for matched navigation and mutation acceptance.

gaps.title: Compiler-free client builds and complete CSP application evidence
gaps.solid: The v2 build/compiler stack is part of the selected comparison input. An application-level CSP claim still requires its emitted graph and runtime behavior.
gaps.purity: strictAot is implemented and checks failed transforms plus retained Purity client compiler paths. Five paired production AOT fixtures exist; SSR compiler support is legitimate. The bundle fixture runner rejects dynamic imports.
gaps.impact: A compiler-free positioning needs proof across real lazy routes, islands and dependencies, beyond static fixture sizes.
acceptance: Install candidate or published packages outside the monorepo and build client/SSR/hydration with lazy routes and islands.
Inspect all emitted chunks and exercise the application under its real restrictive CSP.
Keep actionable negative cases and preserve supported server compilation; do not claim to audit arbitrary third-party code.
gaps.nextSlice: Extend installed-consumer acceptance to one strict-AOT lazy application and archive its complete chunk inventory.

gaps.title: Source/owner diagnostics and predictable HMR
gaps.solid: The v2 development surface includes source attribution, owner/graph diagnostics and compiler-provided source locations. Exact HMR behavior belongs to the selected tooling.
gaps.purity: The graph inspector and development panel expose values/dependencies but no source locations or component tree. Source-map and route HMR paths exist; a complete owner/resource application HMR journey is not established.
gaps.impact: A stale view is harder to trace to its creation site and owning component; edits need explicit state/cleanup expectations.
acceptance: Find a seeded stale binding's source and owner through the debugger in a real transformed application.
Edit a component, route and shared state while requests/listeners/effects are active; document preserve-state versus reload behavior.
Verify no duplicate work and no diagnostics retained in production.
gaps.nextSlice: Add source and owner attribution for one end-to-end debugging journey before considering optional time travel.

gaps.title: Enforced public declaration and negative typing contracts
gaps.solid: Compare actual public declarations and generated route APIs for the pinned v2 stack with an explicitly selected TypeScript version.
gaps.purity: Public declarations and strict scaffold builds exist. Core/plugin tsconfigs exclude tests; ordinary Vitest runs do not type-check compile-shaped cases or enforce their negative assertions.
gaps.impact: A green runtime suite can miss public API type regressions.
acceptance: Run tsc --strict on positive and negative consumers against built/published declarations without source aliases.
Cover overloaded watches, props/slots/events, resources, generated routes and action payloads.
Prove an intended type error makes the negative test pass, and a removed diagnostic makes it fail.
gaps.nextSlice: Create a small declaration-consumer type gate with real negative cases using the existing compiler.

gaps.title: Matched current runtime, allocation, retention and payload evidence
gaps.solid: Performance must be measured for the exact rc.18 application and workload; no release-level universal speed/size claim is used.
gaps.purity: Historical #280 measurements show mixed outcomes at older versions. Row/binding semantic parity and internal bundle/memory gates exist. The normal timing runner does not persist its raw arrays, and no new matched rc.18 result was produced by this audit.
gaps.impact: Without current comparable samples, the next performance optimization has no defensible bottleneck or regression baseline.
acceptance: Pass per-scenario DOM/data/state-strategy parity before timing ordinary lists; keep virtualization separate.
Archive raw samples, dispersion, run order, full environment and separate uninstrumented timing, allocation and retained-heap evidence.
Record initial-route plus full lazy application raw/gzip/Brotli totals and publish regressions as well as improvements.
gaps.nextSlice: Persist existing runner samples after the timed region, refresh a matched rc.18 row/binding baseline, then select one measured bottleneck.

gaps.title: Published consumer, host and accessibility acceptance
gaps.solid: Production-choice comparisons must name the actual package stack, hosts and accessibility journeys. No ecosystem-size or reliability ranking is inferred from package names.
gaps.purity: The audited main is unreleased 0.5.0; registry 0.4.0 client/SSR and candidate tarball app checks have different scopes. Node deployment and isolated Edge checks exist. Per-host live evidence and specified assistive-technology journeys remain incomplete.
gaps.impact: Repository success alone does not establish a usable upgrade and deployment path for the version customers install.
acceptance: Record actual registry/candidate versions, integrity and lockfiles separately, including mixed-delivery consumers and any real app upgrade.
Verify the claimed host's streaming, cancellation, actions, headers and CSP behavior.
Complete or explicitly narrow supported browser/assistive-technology commitments with recorded application journeys.
gaps.nextSlice: Maintain an installed-consumer evidence ledger and add the missing mixed-delivery release journey without publishing automatically.

gaps.title: Public owner composition and external-source lifetime
gaps.solid: v2 exposes owner capture/re-entry and explicitly detached roots. When iteration starts under a live synchronous owner/computation, rc.18 from(source) closes the source on supersession or owner disposal; plain iteration or iteration begun after await relies on iterator closure. Ownership is synchronous on re-entry.
gaps.purity: Automatic component/effect/branch/row ownership and manual stop/dispose exist. General capture/re-entry/detached scope APIs are internal. Per-scope disposer registration order is FIFO, an observable difference from v2 owner LIFO.
gaps.impact: Reusable integrations that create reactive work in later callbacks need manual teardown wiring and a clear contract after parent disposal.
acceptance: A later callback creates work explicitly bound to a live parent and is rejected or safely disposed after that parent dies.
A deliberately detached cache has an explicit lifetime and is released exactly once.
Record nested cleanup order and subscription/iterator teardown under replacement, error and unmount.
gaps.nextSlice: Define the minimal public ownership composition needed by an external subscription adapter; keep cache ownership deliberate.

evidence.scope: Cleanup order for source-free nested Purity watches versus nested Solid roots only. Does not establish Purity component DOM unmount or external-adapter teardown.

dependencyRules: dependsOn constrains whole-row acceptance. Bounded correctness or evidence slices may start earlier when their own inputs are sufficient; finish the active implementation PR before selecting another implementation slice.
